title: Two derivatives of the spectral primitive give an integrable decaying holonomy remainder

primitive_budget.spectral_primitive: Assume the pure-point harmonic-electric sector is absent and F_+,F_- are supported away from omega=0. For arbitrary constant flat holonomy a_infinity, write a(t)=a_infinity+tilde a(t), with G_+=iF_+/omega, G_-=F_-/(i omega), and tilde a(t)=int[e^(it omega)G_+(omega)+e^(-it omega)G_-(omega)]domega, so -partial_t tilde a=E_h.
primitive_budget.weaker_hypothesis: Require G_+,G_- in W^{2,1}, with their values and first derivatives zero at every support endpoint. This is a condition on the divided spectral density F/omega, not K1603's W^{3,1} condition on F.
primitive_budget.decay: Two integrations by parts give |tilde a(t)|<=t^(-2)B_G2 for t>=1, where B_G2=||G_+''||_1+||G_-''||_1; directly |tilde a(t)|<=B_G0=||G_+||_1+||G_-||_1.
primitive_budget.budgets: Therefore ||tilde a||_infinity<=B_G0, int_0^infinity|tilde a|dt<=B_G0+B_G2, and int_0^infinity|tilde a|^2dt<=B_G0(B_G0+B_G2). The oscillatory remainder tends to zero while a_infinity may be nonzero.
primitive_budget.scope_guard: The theorem controls the holonomy primitive required by the K1598 normal form. It does not prove E_h in L1, derive the atom-free representation from nonlinear dynamics, control curvature/current/radial remainders, or construct a source-owned flow.
